akhfash:4-4.t: He said ﴿بَلَىٰ قَادِرِينَ عَلَىٰ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ﴾, that is: (able) to gather (أَنْ نَجْمعَ); that is: "yes, We gather them, being able" (بَلَى نَجْمَعُها قادِرِين). The singular of "البَنَان" (fingertips) is بَنَانَة.

akhfash:10-10.t:
And He said ﴿أَيْنَ ٱلْمَفَرُّ﴾, that is: where is the fleeing (الفِرار)? The poet said [in the madīd metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-third verse cited as evidence]:
يا لَبَكْرِ أنْشرُوا لِي كُلَيْبَاً * يا لَبَكْرِ أَيْنَ أَيْنَ الفِرار
(O clan of Bakr, bring Kulayb back to life for me! O clan of Bakr, where, where is the flight?)
Because every maṣdar (verbal noun) built on this pattern is made "مَفْعَل"; and when He means the place, He says ﴿المَفِرّ﴾. It has also been read ﴿أَيْنَ المَفِرّ﴾, because everything whose verb is on the pattern "يَفْعِل" has its "مَفْعِل" with kasra, such as "المَضْرِب" when you mean the place in which one strikes.

akhfash:14-14.t: And He said ﴿بَلِ ٱلإِنسَانُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ﴾: He made him himself the evidence (البصيرة), as you say to a man "أَنْتَ حُجَّةٌ على نَفْسِكَ" ("you are a proof against yourself").

akhfash:22-23.t: [And] He said ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ﴾, that is: beautiful; ﴿إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ﴾: by looking to Allah He means — and Allah knows best — (looking) to what comes to them of His blessings and provision. And you may say "وَاللهِ ما أَنْظُرُ إِلاَّ إِلَى اللهِ وإِلَيْكَ" ("by Allah, I look only to Allah and to you"), that is: I await what is with Allah and what is with you.

akhfash:31-31.t: And He said ﴿فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صَلَّىٰ﴾, that is: he did not believe and did not pray (فَلَمْ يصدّق ولم يصلّ), as you say "ذَهَبَ فَلاَ جاءَني ولا جاءَك" ("he went away, and came neither to me nor to you").

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿عَلَىٰ أَن يُحْيِـيَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾; and some read ﴿يُحيِ الموتى﴾, concealing it (ikhfāʾ) and placing it between assimilation (idghām) and non-assimilation. It is not correct for it to be assimilated here, because the final yāʾ does not remain in one state, [since] it becomes an alif in your saying "يَحْيَا" and is dropped in the jussive. So assimilation is not binding on it, and nothing is possible in it except ikhfāʾ (concealment), which is between idghām and clear pronunciation (bayān).

daas-irab:1-2.t: ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ﴾ redundant (zāʾida), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿بِيَوْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلا أُقْسِمُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿بِالنَّفْسِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿اللَّوَّامَةِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa).

daas-irab:3-4.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسانُ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿أن﴾ lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); and ﴿لن نَجْمَعَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); and ﴿عِظامَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the lightened an, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يحسب; and ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer; and ﴿قادِرِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition; and ﴿أَنْ نُسَوِّيَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative by an, whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿بَنانَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by ʿalā, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) قادرين.

daas-irab:5-6.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī); and ﴿يُرِيدُ الْإِنْسانُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿لِيَفْجُرَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl); and ﴿أَمامَهُ﴾ an adverb of place; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. And ﴿يَسْئَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); and ﴿أَيَّانَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); and ﴿يَوْمُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾; the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of يسأل, and the clause «يسأل..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-10.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; and ﴿إذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَخَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿جُمِعَ﴾ a passive past verb; and ﴿الشَّمْسُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and ﴿الْقَمَرُ﴾ conjoined to الشمس; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَقُولُ الْإِنْسانُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ يوم is an adverb of time annexed to its like; and ﴿أَيْنَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); and ﴿الْمَفَرُّ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:11-13.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr); and ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation; and ﴿وَزَرَ﴾ its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. And ﴿إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar; and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb of time annexed to its like; and ﴿الْمُسْتَقَرُّ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. And ﴿يُنَبَّؤُا﴾ a passive imperfect verb; and ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive; and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb annexed to its like; and ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿قَدَّمَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿وَأَخَّرَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to قدم.

daas-irab:14-15.t: ﴿بَلِ﴾ a particle of digression and transition (iḍrāb wa-intiqāl); and ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿عَلى نَفْسِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿بَصِيرَةٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لَوْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida); and ﴿أَلْقى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مَعاذِيرَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:16-17.t: ﴿لا تُحَرِّكْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿لِسانَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; and ﴿لِتَعْجَلَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl), and the fāʿil is latent; and ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to تحرك. And ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb; and ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; and ﴿جَمْعَهُ﴾ its postponed noun; and ﴿قُرْآنَهُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; the clause is causal (taʿlīl) to the prohibition, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-19.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; and ﴿إذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿قَرَأْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation; and ﴿فَاتَّبِعْ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); and ﴿قُرْآنَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. And ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; and ﴿إِنَّ عَلَيْنا بَيانَهُ﴾ parsed like «إن علينا جمعه».

daas-irab:20-21.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr); and ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb); and ﴿تُحِبُّونَ الْعاجِلَةَ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿تَذَرُونَ الْآخِرَةَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:22-25.t: ﴿وُجُوهٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb annexed to its like; and ﴿ناضِرَةٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿إِلى رَبِّها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second khabar. ﴿ناظِرَةٌ﴾ a second khabar. ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ باسِرَةٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. And ﴿تَظُنُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿أَنْ يُفْعَلَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an; and ﴿بِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿فاقِرَةٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb stands in place of the two objects of تظن, and the verbal clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of وجوه.

daas-irab:26-30.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr); and ﴿إِذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿بَلَغَتِ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿التَّراقِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَقِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb; and ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿راقٍ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause «قيل..» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَظَنَّ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ anna and its noun; and ﴿الْفِراقُ﴾ its khabar; the interpreted maṣdar stands in place of the two objects of ظن, and the clause «ظن..» is conjoined to what precedes it. And ﴿وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿بِالسَّاقِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. And ﴿إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾ a fronted khabar; and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb of time annexed to its like; and ﴿الْمَساقُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:31-35.t: ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; and ﴿لا﴾ negative; and ﴿صَدَّقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿وَلا صَلَّى﴾ conjoined to «فلا صدق». ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ a particle of rectification (istidrāk); and ﴿كَذَّبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾ conjoined to كذب. And ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; and ﴿ذَهَبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿إِلى أَهْلِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿يَتَمَطَّى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And ﴿أَوْلى﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿لَكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; and ﴿فَأَوْلى﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; and ﴿أَوْلى﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; the clause is resumptive; and ﴿ثُمَّ أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى﴾ is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:36-37.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسانُ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿أَنْ يُتْرَكَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir) [Translator's note: so in the source; for a passive verb this is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]; the clause is resumptive. ﴿سُدىً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb stands in place of the two objects of يحسب. And ﴿أَلَمْ يَكُ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and its noun is latent; and ﴿نُطْفَةً﴾ khabar (predicate); and ﴿مِنْ مَنِيٍّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of نطفة; and ﴿يُمْنى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent; the clause is an adjective (naʿt).

daas-irab:38-39.t:
﴿ثُمَّ كانَ﴾ a conjunction, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿عَلَقَةً﴾ khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.
And ﴿فَخَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَسَوَّى﴾ conjoined to فخلق; and ﴿فَجَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿الزَّوْجَيْنِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿الذَّكَرَ﴾ badal (substitute) of الزوجين; and ﴿الْأُنْثى﴾ conjoined to الذكر.

daas-irab:40-40.t: ﴿أَلَيْسَ ذلِكَ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the demonstrative is its noun; and ﴿بِقادِرٍ﴾ genitive (majrūr) in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position as the khabar (predicate) of laysa; the clause is resumptive; and ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition; and ﴿أَنْ يُحْيِيَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative by an, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿الْمَوْتى﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by the preposition, and both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) قادر.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَاهُ [فَٱتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ]﴾.
When Gabriel, peace be upon him, recites it to you, "فاتبع قرآنه" (then follow its recitation). القراءة and القرآن are both maṣdars (verbal nouns), just as you say: راجحٌ بيِّن الرجحان والرجوح (clearly preponderant, رجحان and رجوح), and المعرفة and العرفان, and الطواف and الطوفان.

farraa:20-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ﴾. ﴿وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلآخِرَةَ﴾.
It has been transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him: "بَلْ تُحِبُّون، وتَذَرُون" with tāʾ, and many read it "بل يحبون" with yāʾ. The Qur'an sometimes addresses those to whom it was sent down directly, and at other times treats them as absent, as in His saying: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا كُنْتُمْ فى الْفُلْكِ وجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ﴾.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يُوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ﴾.
Radiant with bliss.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ﴾.
الفاقرة is the calamity (الداهية). The names of the Resurrection and of the punishment have come with the meanings of calamities and with their names.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ ٱلتَّرَاقِيَ﴾.
He says: when a man's soul reaches his collarbones (تراقيه) at death, and those around him say: "مَنْ رَاقٍ؟" — is there [any] healer? Is there any charmer (راق)? — and the man thinks "أنه الفراق", i.e. he knows that it is the parting. It is also said: "Is there any راق" because the Angel of Death has angels with him, and when the dying man gives up [117/a] his soul, some of them say to others: "Which of you will ascend (يرقى) with it?" — from رقيت, meaning: I ascended.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْتَفَّتِ ٱلسَّاقُ بِٱلسَّاقِ﴾.
The first hardship of the affair of the Hereafter came upon him together with the hardest, last part of the affair of this world; that is His saying: ﴿وَٱلْتَفَّتِ ٱلسَّاقُ بِٱلسَّاقِ﴾. It is also said: his two shanks were wound together, just as it is said of a woman whose thighs touch each other: she is لَفّاء.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَتَمَطَّىٰ﴾.
He struts; because the back is the مَطا, so he twists his back in strutting. This is specifically about Abū Jahl.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِّن مَّنِيٍّ يُمْنَىٰ﴾.
With yāʾ and with tāʾ. Whoever says يُمنَى refers it to the مني (semen), and تُمنى refers it to the نطفة (drop). Both are correct. The companions of ʿAbdullāh [ibn Masʿūd] read it with tāʾ, and some of the people of Medina [also] with tāʾ.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَن يُحْيِـيَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾.
You pronounce both yāʾs distinctly, giving the first a kasra, with the ḥāʾ vowelless. If you give the ḥāʾ a kasra and transfer to it the vowel of the first yāʾ that follows it, that is correct, as the poet said:
وكأنها بين النساء سبيكة * تمشى بِسُدَّةِ بيتها فتَعَىّ
(As though, among the women, she were an ingot [of silver], walking in the porch of her house and growing weary.)
He meant: فتعيا.

farraa:1-1.t:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: I heard al-Farrāʾ say: His saying: ﴿لاَ أُقْسِمُ﴾ — many of the grammarians used to say: (لا) is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant). Al-Farrāʾ said: One does not begin with a negation and then make it a connective intended to be discarded; for if this were permitted, a statement containing a negation could not be distinguished from a statement containing none. Rather, the Qur'an came as a rebuttal of those who denied the Resurrection, Paradise and the Fire, so the oath came as a rebuttal of them in much speech, both what begins [a discourse] and what does not — like your saying in speech: لا والله لا أفعل ذاك (No, by Allah, I will not do that). They made (لا), even when you see it at the beginning, a rejection of speech that has preceded. If you dropped (لا) from what is intended as a reply, there would be no difference between an oath that is a reply and an oath that begins afresh. Do you not see that you say, beginning: والله إن الرسول لحق (By Allah, the Messenger is true); but when you say: لا والله إن الرسول لحق (No, by Allah, the Messenger is true), it is as if you were giving the lie to people who denied it? This is the aspect of (لا) with oaths, and with all oaths in every place where you see (لا) placed at the beginning; and it is frequent in speech.
Someone who did not know this aspect, as you see [115/a], used to read: "لأقسم بيوم القيامة" — it is reported of al-Ḥasan — making it a lām prefixed to أقسم; and that is correct, because the Arabs say: لأحلف بالله ليكونن كذا وكذا (I shall swear by Allah that such and such will surely happen), making it a lām without the meaning of لا.
[Translator's note: «هذا الوجاز» is as printed, evidently for «هذا جاز» ("this were permitted").]

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَيْنَ ٱلْمَفَرُّ﴾.
The people read المفر with fatḥa on the fāʾ. [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us, he said:] And he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Yaḥyā ibn Salama ibn Kuhayl told me, from his father, from a man, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: "أين المفِر", and said: المفَر is only the flight-place of the animal, where it flees. They are two dialect forms: المفِر and المفَر, المدِبّ and المدَبّ. Whatever has a kasra in its yafʿilu form, like يدِب, يفِر and يصِح, the Arabs say [its noun of place as]: مَفِر and مفَر, مصِح and مَصَح, مَدِب and مَدَب. One of them recited to me:
كأن بقَايا الأثر فوقَ متونه * مَدب الدَّبى فوق النقا وهو سارِح
(As if the traces of the [sword's] grain on its blades were the creeping-track of young locusts over the sand-dune as they roam.)
They recite it مَدَب, which is more frequent than مَدِب. One says: جاء على مَدَب السيل and مدِب السيل (he came along the flood's course), and ما فى قميصه مَصِح ولا مَصَحٌّ (there is no sound place in his shirt).

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ لاَ وَزَرَ﴾.
الوزر is a refuge.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُنَبَّأُ ٱلإِنسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِمَا قَدَّمَ﴾.
He means: what he sent ahead of his deeds, and what he left behind of a practice (sunna) that he left to be acted upon after him. If he established a good practice, he has the like [of the reward] of those who act on it, without their being diminished; and if it was an evil practice, he is punished for it, without anything being diminished from the punishment of those who act on it.
[Translator's note: «بعمل بها» is as printed, for «يُعمل بها» ("to be acted upon").]

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلِ ٱلإِنسَانُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ﴾.
He is saying: over man there are watchers from his own self who bear witness against him about his deeds: the hands, the feet, the eyes and the private part. The poet said:
كأنَّ على ذى الظن عيناً بصيرةً * بمقعَدِه أو منظرٍ هو ناظرُه
يُحاذِرُ حتى يحسِبُ الناسَ كلَّهم * من الخوفِ لا تخفى عليهم سرائرُه
(It is as if over the suspicious man there were a watchful eye, at his seat or at any sight he beholds; he is so wary that out of fear he reckons all people to be people from whom his secrets are not hidden.)

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ أَلْقَىٰ مَعَاذِيرَهُ﴾.
It has come in the interpretation: even if he lets down his curtains. And it has come: even if he makes excuses, there is over him one who will give the lie to his excuse.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying [116/b], Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسَانَكَ﴾.
When Jibrīl ﷺ came down with the revelation to Muḥammad ﷺ with the Qur'an, he would recite part of it to himself before it was complete, for fear of forgetting it. So it was said to him: ﴿لاَ تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا جَمْعَهُ﴾ in your heart ﴿وَقُرْآنَهُ﴾ and its recitation; i.e. Jibrīl, peace be upon him, will repeat it to you.
[Translator's note: the one who "would recite part of it to himself" is the Prophet ﷺ, as the address that follows shows.]

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلنَّفْسِ ٱللَّوَّامَةِ﴾.
There is no soul, righteous or wicked, but that it blames itself: if it has done good, it says: Why did I not do more? And if it has done evil, it says: Would that I had held back! Would that I had not done it!

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلَىٰ قَادِرِينَ عَلَىٰ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ﴾.
It has come in the interpretation: Yes, We are able to make his fingertips even, i.e. to make his fingers solid, not separated, like a camel's hoof. So He said: Yes, [We are] able to restore the smallest bones as they were. His saying "قادرين" is accusative as departing from "نجمع" [i.e. as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the subject of نجمع], as if you said in speech: أتحسب أن لن نقوى عليك، بلى قادرين على أقوى منك (Do you think we will not overpower you? Yes, [we are] able [to overpower] one stronger than you). He means: yes, we will overpower, being able; yes, we will overpower, being capable of more than this. Had it been nominative as a fresh start, as if He said: بلى نحن قادرون على أكثر من ذا (yes, We are able to do more than this), it would be correct.
As for people's saying: [the underlying form is] بلى نقدر, and when it was turned into قادرين it became accusative — that is a mistake, because a verb is not made accusative by converting it from yafʿalu to fāʿil. Do you not see that you say: أتقوم إلينا (will you rise to [come to] us?), and if you convert it to the fāʿil form you say: أقائم, and it would be a mistake to say: أقائماً أنت إِلينا؟ They used to cite as proof the saying of al-Farazdaq:
على قسَمٍ لا أشتم الدهر مسلما * ولا خارجا مِنْ فىَّ زورُ كلام
(Upon an oath that I will never revile a Muslim, nor shall false speech come out of my mouth.)
They said: he only meant لا أشتم and ولا يخرج, and when he turned it into خارج he made it accusative. But he made it accusative only because he meant: عاهدتُ ربى لا شاتما أحدا ولا خارجاً من فىّ زور كلام (I have pledged to my Lord, not reviling anyone and no false speech coming out of my mouth). And his saying لا أشتم is in the position of the accusative [115/b].

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us,] he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Qays told me, from Abū Ḥaṣīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ ٱلإِنسَانُ لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ﴾; he said: He says: I will repent later, I will repent later. And al-Kalbī said: he multiplies sins and puts off repentance.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا بَرِقَ ٱلْبَصَرُ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, al-Ḥasan and some of the people of Medina read it (بَرِق) with kasra on the rāʾ, and Nāfiʿ al-Madanī read it: "فإِذ بَرَق البصر" with fatḥa on the rāʾ, from البريق (glitter): it stares, for whoever reads with fatḥa. And his saying "بَرِق" [means]: it is terrified. One of the Arabs recited to me:
نَعَانِى حَنانةُ طُوبالةً * تُسَفُّ يَبيسًا من العِشْرِقِ
فنفسَكَ فَانْعَ ولا تَنْعَنِى * وداوِ الكُلُومَ ولا تَبْرَقِ
(Ḥanāna announced my death — a ewe fed on dry ʿishriq. Announce your own death, not mine; treat the wounds and do not be terrified.)
He gave the rāʾ fatḥa, i.e.: do not be terrified by the horror of the wounds you have; likewise the sight will be terrified on the Day of Resurrection.
And whoever reads "بَرَق" says: he opened his eyes [wide]; and his sight also glitters because of that.
[Translator's note: «فإِذ» is as printed (for «فإذا»), and «بَرق» glossed as "terrified" is to be read بَرِق. «تَبْرَقِ» in the verse is the imperfect of بَرِق, hence "he gave the rāʾ fatḥa". «يرق بصره» is as printed, for «برق بصره» ("his sight glitters").]

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَخَسَفَ ٱلْقَمَرُ﴾.
Its light has gone.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجُمِعَ ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ﴾.
[In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh:] وجمع بين الشمس والقمر — He means: [joined] also in the loss of their light, so there is no light for this one nor for that one. Its meaning is: He joined them together in the loss of light, as you say: هذا يوم يستوى فيه الأعمى والبصير (this is a day in which the blind and the seeing are equal), i.e. both of them are blind in it. It is also said: they are brought together like two hamstrung bulls in the Fire. He said جُمِع and did not say جمعت for this reason: because the meaning is "He joined between them"; this is one way. Or, if you wish, you may take both of them in the sense of two lights, as if you said: the two lights were joined, the two radiances were joined; that is the view of al-Kisāʾī. Some people used to say: the verb of the sun was made masculine only because it is not singled out by [the verb] جُمع until something else shares it; so when a masculine noun shares it, the expression for both is جُمِعا, and جمعتا is not used. It was said to them: How do you say "the sun [116/a] was joined, and the moon"? They said: جُمِعت; and so they retracted that view.
[Translator's note: «ثورين» ("two bulls") in «فى مذهب ثورين» is as printed; the sense requires «نورين» ("two lights"), which is how the following sentence explains it.]

zajjaj:22-22.t: His saying: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ ناضِرَةٌ﴾ ﴿إلى رَبِّها ناظِرَةٌ﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 23]: they are made radiant by the bliss of the Garden and by looking at their Lord. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿تَعْرِفُ في وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 24].

zajjaj:24-25.t: ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ باسِرَةٌ﴾ ﴿تَظُنُّ أنْ يُفْعَلَ بِها فاقِرَةٌ﴾: «باسِرَةٌ» means loathsome and scowling, having become certain that the punishment is descending upon them. The meaning of ﴿تَظُنُّ أنْ يُفْعَلَ بِها فاقِرَةٌ﴾ is: they are certain that a calamity of punishment will be done to them.

zajjaj:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿كَلا﴾: «كَلّا» is a word of deterrence (radʿ) and warning, and its meaning is: "Desist from what leads to the punishment."
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إذا بَلَغَتِ التَّراقِيَ﴾: Allah reminded them of the hardship of the first of the days of the Hereafter, when the soul reaches the collarbone (al-tarquwa).

zajjaj:27-27.t: ﴿وَقِيلَ مَن راقٍ﴾, that is: who can cure from this state? And this — and Allah knows best — is what one says in despair, that is: who is able to save by incantation (yarqī) from death? And it was said in the exegesis: ﴿مَن راقٍ﴾ means: who will ascend (yarqā) with his soul — the angels of mercy or the angels of punishment?

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿وَظَنَّ أنَّهُ الفِراقُ﴾, that is: and the one whose soul reaches his collarbones became certain that he is parting from this world.

zajjaj:29-29.t: ﴿والتَفَّتِ السّاقُ بِالسّاقِ﴾: at death the shin clings to the shin. It was said: "The last hardship of this world was wound together with the first hardship of the Hereafter."

zajjaj:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿فَلا صَدَّقَ ولا صَلّى﴾: by this is meant Abū Jahl ibn Hishām. It has come in the exegesis: every community has a Pharaoh, and the Pharaoh of this community is Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.

zajjaj:33-33.t: ﴿ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إلى أهْلِهِ يَتَمَطّى﴾: its meaning is "with a swaggering gait"; it is taken from «اَلْمَطا», which is the back.

zajjaj:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿أوْلى لَكَ فَأوْلى﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: what is hateful has come close to you, O Abū Jahl. The Arabs say: «أوْلى لِفُلانٍ» ("woe draws near to so-and-so") when they invoke something hateful against him.

zajjaj:36-36.t: ﴿أيَحْسَبُ الإنْسانُ أنْ يُتْرَكَ سُدًى﴾, that is: that he will be left neither commanded nor forbidden. Then He pointed them to the resurrection by His power over the first creation, saying: ﴿ألَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِن مَنِيٍّ يُمْنى﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 37]. It was also read «تُمْنى». Whoever read «تُمْنى» did so in agreement with the word النُّطْفَة (feminine), and whoever read ﴿يُمْنى﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 37] did so in agreement with the word مَنِيّ (masculine).

zajjaj:38-39.t: ﴿ثُمَّ كانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوّى﴾ ﴿فَجَعَلَ مِنهُ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ والأُنْثى﴾. Then He made them acknowledge it, saying: ﴿ألَيْسَ ذَلِكَ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أنْ يُحْيِيَ المَوْتى﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 40].

zajjaj:1-2.t:
Sūrat al-Qiyāma
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾ ﴿وَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوّامَةِ﴾ ("Nay, I swear by the Day of Resurrection, and nay, I swear by the self-reproaching soul"). There is no disagreement among people that its meaning is "I swear by the Day of Resurrection", but they differed about the explanation of «لا». Some of them said: «لا» is void (laghw), even though it comes at the beginning of the sura, because the whole Qur'an is like a single sura, since it is connected, part with part; so «لا» here was treated like it is in His saying ﴿لِئَلا يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 29] ("so that the People of the Book may know"). And some grammarians said: «لا» is a rejection of their speech, as though they denied the raising, so it was said: "No, the matter is not as you have stated; I swear by the Day of Resurrection."
And His saying ﴿إنَّكم مَبْعُوثُونَ﴾ [Hūd: 7] ("Indeed, you will be raised") indicates the answer [to the oath].
[Translator's note: the quoted words are from Hūd 7, cited as indicating the omitted answer of the oath here, which would be something like "you will surely be raised".]

zajjaj:10-10.t:
﴿يَقُولُ الإنْسانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ أيْنَ المَفَرُّ﴾ ("Man will say on that Day: Where is the escape?"); it is also read «أيْنَ المَفِرُّ» with kasra on the fāʾ. Whoever reads with fatḥa, it is in the meaning "Where is the fleeing?"; and whoever reads with kasra, it is on the meaning "Where is the place of fleeing?" The mafʿal [form] from [verbs] like «جَلَسْتُ» has fatḥa on the ʿayn [of the pattern], and so does the maṣdar (verbal noun): you say «جَلَسْتُ مَجْلَسًا» with fatḥa on the lām, meaning "a sitting (julūsan)"; and when you say «جَلَسْتُ مَجْلِسًا», you mean the place.
[Translator's note: as printed, the sentence on the mafʿal form is compressed; the examples show that the verbal noun takes fatḥa (majlas) and the noun of place kasra (majlis).]

zajjaj:11-11.t: Then He, the Exalted, made known that they have no stronghold and no escape, and said: ﴿كَلا لا وزَرَ﴾ ("No! There is no refuge"). «الوَزَر» in the speech of the Arabs is the mountain in which refuge is sought; this is its root meaning, and everything in which you take refuge and by which you escape is a «وَزَر».

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿بَلِ الإنْسانُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ﴾ ﴿وَلَوْ ألْقى مَعاذِيرَهُ﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 15] ("Rather, man will be a witness against himself, even if he presents his excuses"): its meaning is "Rather, man — his limbs will testify against him." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ ألْسِنَتُهم وأيْدِيهِمْ وأرْجُلُهم بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [al-Nūr: 24] ("On a Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them as to what they used to do"); and He said in another place: ﴿حَتّى إذا ما جاءُوها شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ سَمْعُهم وأبْصارُهم وجُلُودُهم بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 20] ("until, when they reach it, their hearing, their eyes and their skins will testify against them as to what they used to do"). So Allah made known that these limbs with which they act are witnesses against them.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ ألْقى مَعاذِيرَهُ﴾ ("even if he presents his excuses"): even if he put forward every argument he has. It has come in the exegesis: «المَعاذِير» are the curtains; the singular is «مِعْذار».

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿لا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ﴾ ("Do not move your tongue with it to hasten with it"): when Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended with revelation to the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet (peace be upon him) would recite it along with him, for fear that it would escape him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He would not make him forget it, and that He would gather it in his heart, and said: ﴿إنَّ عَلَيْنا جَمْعَهُ وقُرْآنَهُ﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 17] ("Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation"), i.e. it is upon Us to make you recite so that you will not forget, and upon Us is its recitation to you.

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿فَإذا قَرَأْناهُ فاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ﴾ ("So when We have recited it, follow its recitation"), i.e. do not hasten with the recitation until what is being revealed at its time has been recited to you.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إنَّ عَلَيْنا بَيانَهُ﴾ ("Then upon Us is its clarification"), i.e. it is upon Us to send it down as an Arabic Qur'an without any crookedness, in which there is clarification for people.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلى قادِرِينَ﴾ ("Yes, [We are] able"): the meaning is "Yes, We shall surely gather you, being able"; the meaning is: "I swear by the Day of Resurrection and the self-reproaching soul: We shall surely gather them (i.e. the bones), being able to restore his fingertips." It has come in the exegesis: "Yes, We are able to make it like the hoof of a camel." But what fits better with the gathering of the bones is: "Yes, We shall gather them, being able to restore his fingertips as they were, even though their bones are few and small and decay has reached them."
«النَّفْسُ اللَّوّامَةُ» ("the self-reproaching soul"): its explanation is that every soul will reproach its owner in the Hereafter: if he did evil, his soul will reproach him, and if he did good, it will reproach him for not doing more of it.

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ الإنْسانُ لِيَفْجُرَ أمامَهُ﴾ ("Rather, man desires to continue in sin before him"): its meaning is that he keeps postponing repentance and putting forward evil deeds. It is possible — and Allah knows best — that its meaning is "to disbelieve in what is ahead of him", and the evidence for that is His saying: ﴿يَسْألُ أيّانَ يَوْمُ القِيامَةِ﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 6] ("He asks: When is the Day of Resurrection?"). So «يَفْجُرَ أمامَهُ» on this [view] — and Allah knows best — means he denies what is ahead of him of the raising.

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا بَرِقَ البَصَرُ﴾ ("So when the sight is dazzled"); it is also read «بَرَقَ البَصَرُ». Whoever reads ﴿بَرِقَ﴾, its meaning is: it is terrified and bewildered; and whoever reads «بَرَقَ», it is from «بَرَقَ، يَبْرُقُ», from the glitter (barīq) of the eyes.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿وَخَسَفَ القَمَرُ﴾ ("and the moon is eclipsed"), i.e. the light of the moon departs.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿وَجُمِعَ الشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ﴾ ("and the sun and the moon are joined"), i.e. they are joined in the departure of their light.
